title: Extension of a projective chart equation after a coordinate power
statement:
Let $R$ be a commutative ring, $n\geq0$, and $B=R[z_0,\ldots,z_n]$ with each variable of degree one. Put $P=\operatorname{Proj}(B)$ [def-pc-proj], $U_j=D_+(z_j)=\operatorname{Spec}(A_j)$ with $A_j=B_{(z_j),0}$ [def-nagata-homogeneous-localization-degree-zero], and let $i:Z\hookrightarrow P$ be any closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion]. For $0\leq j\leq n$ set $Z_j=i^{-1}(U_j)$, and let $J_j$ be the kernel of $A_j\to\Gamma(Z_j,\mathcal O_Z)$. Fix $a\in\{0,\ldots,n\}$. For every $f\in J_a$ there exist integers $d,N\geq0$ and a homogeneous polynomial $F\in B_d$ such that $f=F/z_a^d$ in $A_a$ and, for every $0\leq j\leq n$, the function
$$\frac{z_a^N F}{z_j^{d+N}}\in A_j$$
restricts to zero in $\Gamma(Z_j,\mathcal O_Z)$. In particular the same function on $U_a$ is $f=(z_a^NF)/z_a^{d+N}$. Vanishing here is equality of sections, including their nilpotent information; no reducedness, nonemptiness, Noetherian or finite-presentation assumption is imposed on $R$ or $Z$.

source.place: Tag 03GL, lemma-closed-in-projective-space, proof: converse J subset J', homogenization of f, the powers T_0^{d_i}, and the maximum over the standard charts.

proof.text: By [def-nagata-homogeneous-localization-degree-zero], choose $d\geq0$ and $F\in B_d$ representing $f$ as $F/z_a^d$. This includes $f=0$, for which $d=0,F=0$ is permitted. Put $h_j=F/z_j^d\in A_j$ for each $j$.

source.place: Tag 03GL, lemma-closed-in-projective-space, proof: converse J subset J', homogenization of f, the powers T_0^{d_i}, and the maximum over the standard charts.

proof.text: Write $C_j=\Gamma(Z_j,\mathcal O_Z)$ and $q_j:A_j\to C_j$. By the affine description in [def-weil-closed-immersion], $Z_j\cong\operatorname{Spec}(A_j/J_j)$ over $U_j$, so $Z_j$ is affine and $C_j\cong A_j/J_j$. Put $t_j=z_a/z_j\in A_j$ and $s_j=q_j(t_j)$. By [lem-weil-pbc-proj-basic-open-intersection], $U_j\cap U_a$ is the principal open $D_{U_j}(t_j)$. Applying [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-into-affine-scheme] to $Z_j\to U_j$ identifies its preimage $Z_j\cap Z_a$ with the principal open $D_{Z_j}(s_j)$. By clause (0) of [lem-weil-pbc-affine-ideals-closed-subscheme], the restriction $C_j\to\Gamma(Z_j\cap Z_a,\mathcal O_Z)$ is a localization at $s_j$. All these statements apply to empty affine schemes as well.

source.place: Tag 03GL, lemma-closed-in-projective-space, proof: converse J subset J', homogenization of f, the powers T_0^{d_i}, and the maximum over the standard charts.

proof.text: On $U_j\cap U_a$, restrictions are the graded localization maps of [def-pc-proj]. The fraction identity there is $h_j=t_j^d f$: both sides are $F/z_j^d$, since $(z_a/z_j)^d(F/z_a^d)=F/z_j^d$. Restrict this equality along $Z_j\cap Z_a\to U_j\cap U_a$. Because $f\in J_a$, the image of $f$ in $\Gamma(Z_a,\mathcal O_Z)$, and hence on $Z_j\cap Z_a$, is zero. Thus $q_j(h_j)$ restricts to zero on $Z_j\cap Z_a$. This is equality of actual sections, not vanishing in residue fields.

source.place: Tag 03GL, lemma-closed-in-projective-space, proof: converse J subset J', homogenization of f, the powers T_0^{d_i}, and the maximum over the standard charts.

proof.text: The localization in Step 2 and [def-weil-ring-localization-away] imply that for each $j$ some $e_j\geq0$ satisfies $s_j^{e_j}q_j(h_j)=0$ in $C_j$: use the defining fraction relation $q_j(h_j)/1=0/1$. Consequently $q_j(t_j^{e_j}h_j)=0$. The identity $t_j^{e_j}h_j=z_a^{e_j}F/z_j^{d+e_j}$ is multiplication of fractions. For $j=a$ one may choose $e_a=0$ because $h_a=f\in J_a$.

source.place: Tag 03GL, lemma-closed-in-projective-space, proof: converse J subset J', homogenization of f, the powers T_0^{d_i}, and the maximum over the standard charts.

proof.text: Choose $N=\max\{e_0,\ldots,e_n\}$, which exists because $n\geq0$ and the index set is finite and nonempty. For each $j$, $q_j(t_j^Nh_j)=s_j^{N-e_j}\bigl(s_j^{e_j}q_j(h_j)\bigr)=0$. But $t_j^Nh_j=z_a^NF/z_j^{d+N}$, as required, and $z_a^NF$ is homogeneous of degree $d+N$. On $U_a$, $z_a^NF/z_a^{d+N}=F/z_a^d=f$. For $n=0$ take $N=0$; for $Z_j=\varnothing$ its section ring is the zero ring and the same equalities hold. The proof uses no reducedness, Noetherianity or finite-presentation hypothesis.
